text:
Matt Coronato is the most interesting puzzle on Calgary's forward list. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking rated his chances from in front of the net in the 98th percentile among forwards last season, and his passing (9.6 primary shot assists per 60) in the 93rd. Yet Evolving-Hockey put him at -1.7 wins above replacement, because opponents got more chances with him on the ice than with almost any forward in the league (bottom 1 percent).

This season looks similar. He has 14 points in 17 games, including four in a 6-2 win over Seattle on October 30, but the Flames get only 41.5 percent of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, nearly eight points worse than without him. He has three goals on 3.48 expected, shooting 8.3 percent.

He is pointless in four straight, and the chances have thinned out in that stretch, so this is not just bad luck. He is 23, a former 13th overall pick who came through Harvard, and the offensive tools are real. Watch his defensive minutes; if the Flames shelter him, the points should come back.
headline: Coronato gets to the net, and gives up a lot too
